### Add the private archive of original outputs: spool, journal, verified upload, list and fetch

change `wvpwtwyomouq` · [log `1e85b253070c`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/1e85b253070c79043fc2d3497ba7105bc2aef2a4ee3e2de781ad9cbcbece4f3d.jsonl.gz)

llm-dlc/tools/artifacts.py is the first piece of the process-plumbing brief (llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing.md, section 2). A producer hands the bytes it made to capture before it shortens, replaces or deletes them. They are sealed once into a spool on disk outside the checkout (~/.local/share/in-the-loop/originals), with a full private inventory of every member's path, type, mode, length and SHA-256, and acknowledged only after the intake record and a SQLite journal have them durably. Small files go into bounded packs, large ones into parts, and an append-only file into segments from which any past prefix restores. A restartable uploader commits each attempt before a byte moves, creates each object only if none is there, reads it back with a credential and compares the original bytes with their name, and writes an immutable receipt last, so a fresh machine can rebuild the catalog from the store alone. Ordinary and restricted originals go to separate private R2 buckets; a restricted occurrence is listed in the ordinary one by a stub with no path. list, show and fetch read with the reader's token into a private cache and work offline on a verified hit; missing, pending, restricted or damaged evidence gives a specific unavailable answer. Nothing in the tool deletes a byte, and ITL_ORIGINALS_OFF=1 switches capture off.

Verified by 33 unit tests (llm-dlc/tools/test_artifacts.py): crashes before and after the intake record, after a put and before the receipt, a lease left by a dead worker, two workers on one object, a store that is offline, that loses its answer, that holds other bytes under the same key or a truncated object, a full disk, reused paths, gaps, unsafe manifests and links, and reads from an empty cache and offline. artifacts.py canary passed 11 of 11 checks on the real buckets on 2026-11-21: custody for both classes, a restore from an empty cache, and each token's limits (the ordinary token refused a restricted key, a PUT and a DELETE; the public Worker and the public traces' token read neither class). The contract is in llm-dlc/specification.md, Original outputs; llm-dlc/loops/llm-dlc-process-plumbing-results.md records where the run stands. Nothing calls capture yet: the runner and collector adapters come next.

### Add sync.py checkpoint: one committed revision to origin's develop, forward only, with outgoing-object checks

change `srwzpppxzsxn` · [log `5ce35f7c9691`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/5ce35f7c96910fff53d2472c707a6e927ca2e3e9b21085fc2eb4480a067903e9.jsonl.gz)

llm-dlc/tools/checkpoint.py gives code checkpoints a job of their own, apart from promotion (the brief, section 1). sync.py checkpoint --rev REV resolves REV once to one committed revision, reads the remote's develop and main, and pushes exactly SHA:refs/heads/develop to origin when develop can move forward to it, carrying the commit develop was read at so the push cannot land on a branch that moved. It runs no test, renders no trace file, uploads no log and waits for no job or uploader, and every jj call it makes ignores the working copy, so another session's uncommitted files are neither snapshotted nor moved. --bootstrap creates develop where main is. Any other ref, remote, pattern or force is refused as an argument.

Before anything leaves the machine it reads every git object and commit message the push would expose for the first time, through every outgoing commit and merge parent, and refuses an unresolved conflict, a raw payload path, an unsafe file name, a blob over 16 MiB, a message-less or set-aside commit, a recognisable credential or one of this machine's own secrets or account identifiers anywhere, anything the redactor would still change in a trace file, and a redaction decision no person is recorded as having taken. A scan of the 18 commits then unpushed showed why the context-shaped kinds are refused in trace files only: the home path and the user name occur in 5,153 result and receipt files of the kind main already publishes, and KEY=value in 109 ordinary fixtures. A blob's verdict is kept by its git id under the policy, rules and decisions in force. A push whose answer is lost is settled by reading the remote. The receipt, outside the tree and sealed into the private archive, says which trace logs are public and which pending and what the archive holds on this machine only. After a push, develop@origin counts among jj's immutable heads.

The redactor now also treats the private archive's three R2 tokens as this machine's secrets. Verified by llm-dlc/tools/test_checkpoint.py, 12 tests on real jj repositories with a bare remote: a dirty workspace is checkpointed at its last commit with the foreign files' hashes and the working-copy commit unchanged, a fresh clone reads the code at develop, and the test gate, the session sync and the log upload are each patched to fail if called; a credential in a parent commit is refused though the tip deleted it; an unsafe message, a run record, an environment file, an oversized blob, a bad name, a conflict and a forged allow-list approval are refused with the remote unchanged; --all, --bookmark, --force, --remote, a refspec and a pattern exit 2; a develop that moved elsewhere is never forced; a lost answer is one push. The tests the change selects passed (22 files). llm-dlc/specification.md, Checkpoints, is the contract. The first push to the real develop is the watcher's, at this cycle's end (the user's decision); a rehearsal on the real history against a bare remote follows. The allow list gains one proposal (a82875ef, a made-up home directory in test_vm_inventory.py), for the user to approve.

### Add sync.py promote: a frozen part of develop becomes main, with its logs, originals and test receipt accounted for

change `xuumpxymnysy` · [log `b41a9df5f7f6`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/b41a9df5f7f6ea692511239f0c0ec3e28488e9db1db909a06a0d4d06fe0fe00a.jsonl.gz)

A promotion is now a command of its own (llm-dlc/tools/promote.py, the specification's new Promotions section). It takes a commit that is already on origin's develop, freezes the commits between main and it (merge parents included; what lands on develop later waits for the next promotion), and builds the publication record in a jj workspace of its own, REPO-promote, so it runs from any workspace whatever is uncommitted there. In the candidate the frozen commits' logs are taken from the workspaces that store them, checked and uploaded; every LLM-Trace must then resolve to a published or withdrawn log, and every original of the frozen jobs, sessions and commits must be remote_verified in the private archive or be a job with no original at all, which is counted as a gap. The record is one commit on the frozen commit holding generated files only: the URLs, the index, and llm-dlc/artifacts/YYYY/MM/DD/promotion-ID.json, a summary of at most 64 KiB (llm-dlc/publication-summary.schema.json) that names the private inventory by occurrence and SHA-256.

The gate asks for a passed default run covering the record's tree, and runs it in the candidate when none does. default_run.covers now also passes llm-dlc/artifacts/ and a llm-dlc/README.md that differs only in its generated session table (the page's own text is still covered), so a run of the frozen commit's tree covers the record. The gate's record and log are sealed in the archive and must be verified there before main moves; the receipt is outside the tree. main is pushed only if it is still where the promotion found it, forward only, and a lost answer is settled by reading the remote; develop then goes forward to the record, or takes it in by an ordinary merge when it moved meanwhile. The state of a promotion is kept by base and frozen commit, so the same command continues one that stopped and finishes one whose push went out before its end was written. --dry-run prints the review view (source changes by finished change, the test receipt, decisions, logs and originals by state) and changes nothing.

### Add delegated redaction decisions, switched off: a person can let one run's watcher decide routine findings

change `qktxmywwtmrt` · [log `b7b96e80f04d`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/b7b96e80f04d71245289ca1449aa420dae1bd4793e7f37f1a282f51bd80bdf37.jsonl.gz)

llm-dlc/tools/delegation.py and the specification's new Delegated decisions paragraph under Redaction. Nothing changes until a person turns it on: the watcher asks with sync.py delegate request, the person grants that request from their own terminal, and sync.py delegate off ends it from any shell. The watcher is the client process (Claude Code's or Codex's) that asked, by pid, start time and boot: a command is the watcher's when the nearest client process above it is that one, so an environment variable or a file in the checkout confers nothing, a worker the watcher started is not the watcher, and a watcher that ended decides nothing more.

While it is on the watcher has three commands of its own, spelled apart from the person's so that the project's permission rules for those stay as they are. delegate approve takes allow-list proposals by id with evidence the command checks itself (the value is in a file main publishes, in a committed fixture, is a digest of a committed file, a git object id or a log's name); a stated public origin is recorded as not checked and refused for a long-token; the kinds the redactor removes stay refused. delegate withhold keeps an unpublished log out of publication for good: sealed in the restricted archive, removed, marked withdrawn in its manifest. delegate mask adds a value to this machine's redactions, withholds the unpublished logs that hold it and escalates the published ones. review escalate (anyone) writes one masked record that check warns of until a person closes it. No command prints a value.

Each decision is a line of a record outside every checkout, chained by hash, signed with a key the permission rules deny agents, and sealed into the restricted archive as it grows. check, land, checkpoint and promote count a decision when it is on main, recorded as a person's, or recorded by the watcher with exactly the bytes the file has, under the redaction policy in force, while the delegation is on. A decision now counts as published only on main: before, any immutable commit counted, and commits on develop have been immutable since the checkpoint command. Also here: promote abandons a record it committed and then found wanting, and does not count its own records among a promotion's evidence; the results page records the promotion rehearsal on the real history (25 commits promoted on a bare remote, the checkpoint fix and the three real missing receipts it found), where a commit's 28 s go, and the design of the trace changes that are next.

Verified by test_delegation.py (9 tests: off by default; who the watcher is; an approval with checked evidence; the refusals; a forged entry, changed bytes, an added and an edited record line, a stale policy and delegation off all failing; withholding into restricted custody; masking with one escalation) and by test_costs.py run --changed (25 files passed).

### Render the generated trace files at promotion, not at every commit; make the check after a commit four times faster

change `qvkkkpkzwzxs` · [log `6539b8c25da5`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/6539b8c25da5cf36832489d005548735fe9fa8f7c385e8a9a85d02a0d4a55f4a.jsonl.gz)

An ordinary sync.py commit, and the commit hook, now write the session's manifest alone. Until now each commit also rewrote the session's summary.md and metrics.json and six global files (index.json, the table in llm-dlc/README.md, traces/README.md, traces/metrics.json, traces/loops.json, traces/loops.md): twelve generated files a commit, megabytes of them for a long session, and a conflict in the global ones whenever two lines merged. They are rendered when they are published or asked for: by sync.py promote in its candidate workspace (from each session's stored current log and its manifest, which now records the workspace path a summary shortens file names by), by sync.py push, and on demand by sync.py sync, also spelled sync.py render, and sync.py regenerate. A session's first commit still makes its summary and metrics, so links to them resolve, and a session synced without rendering is rendered by the next sync that renders whether or not it changed. check compares the generated files with their inputs only when asked (check --rendered, as a promotion and a push ask); it always scans them, and always checks manifests, logs and trailers. The specification's Workflow section has a Rendering paragraph.

A new commit carries LLM-Trace: SESSION sha256:LOG and no longer the two link lines above it, LLM-Trace-Summary (a URL on main) and LLM-Trace-Log (the CDN's URL), which were promises about a promotion that had not happened. Commits that have them keep them, no published commit is restamped, and every reader takes either form. sync.py trace REV says what a commit's identifier resolves to now: the session, its summary, and its log, public, withdrawn, or pending and in which workspace it waits.

The check after a commit took about 16 s of a commit's 28 s here. Two things took half of it. check_trailers read a manifest out of the tree of every traced commit there has ever been (1,543 here): it now keeps what it read of immutable commits, by checkout and tools version, and asks jj only for what @ gained since and for the mutable commits; when a recorded head is no longer an immutable ancestor of @, or under --full, everything is read again. And every stored log's .gz bytes were hashed again at each check to find its cache entry: a log is named by its content and never rewritten, so it is now found by path, size, time and inode, except by an upload, which goes by the bytes it sends, and under --full. Measured here, warm: check 4.1 s (trailers 5.7 s to 0.4 s, sessions 9.5 s to 2.6 s).

Verified by test_performance.py (two tests of rendering on demand, two of the trailer and its resolver; the two tests that pinned the old behaviour updated), test_workspaces.py (the cursor on a real jj repository: read once, still judged against the manifests as they are now, dropped when the commit stops being published, not used under a full audit) and test_costs.py run --changed (23 files passed).

### Find a verification job and its result by id, kept flat or under its day: every reader goes through verification/layout.py

change `pptpprnznwsq` · [log `69b6ba95aa44`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/69b6ba95aa44476e56e308e8a9b34089ae617c36b7ece2735132a0b32cd53ab6.jsonl.gz)

The brief's pipeline layout, readers first. verification/layout.py is the one place that knows where a job's specification and its result are: flat (verification/jobs/ID.json, verification/results/ID/), as all 986 are, or under the UTC day the id begins with (verification/jobs/YYYY/MM/DD/ID.json), with one overflow shard for an id without a date. A job is never moved, since the runner tests the commit that last touched its file; a result goes beside its job; identical duplicates resolve to the flat copy and differing ones are named by pipeline.py validate. Results recorded on other heads are recognised in both layouts from a listing of the commit's tree.

Readers moved to it: pipeline.py (the queue, status, collect, commit-paths, report, resubmit, prioritize, validate, the results index, schema references at the new depth), sync.py's loop statistics, cost_inventory.py, conductor.py, brief_run.py, accept.py, claim_history.py, capture.py, vm_inventory.py and promote.py. New jobs still go flat (WRITE = "flat" in layout.py; VERIFY_LAYOUT=shards for one command): the brief migrates readers before writers, and two standing decisions of the user say to add no complexity to pipeline.py and to move no folders, so the switch is one line left for a person after a real promotion. The conductor loads the module only for the one question that needs it, so a copy of the loop's scripts in a checkout without it still answers the others.

Also fixed, found by this very commit: sync.py commit --only named every file it set aside on one jj command line, and 16,000 of them (an example's per-case records, being packed for the next commit) were more than a command line holds. It now names what stays, and prints the first 40 of a long list with the count of the rest.

### Keep an example's per-case records as one pack a folder, read in place; hold the records to a budget in check

change `tkvzqtpykolq` · [log `0e6af0cdfd7d`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/0e6af0cdfd7d56bb0a208b1f98c893bdb955a8081ac5927902743f9f964a196f.jsonl.gz)

The records' rule of VF-053 (the user's decision 5: seal the records, show 359 restores, then slim them by rule). A native-selector run writes two files for each admitted selector; over examples 340 to 359 that was 16,376 of the 22,103 files their records held, one folder with 2,865 entries. examples/tools/targets/case_pack.py keeps such a folder as cases.tar.gz beside where it was: the same bytes under the same names, written so that the same files give the same pack. The validator (native_selectors.validate_result) reads a case from the folder or from the pack and compares its digest either way, so a plain checkout checks every case as before and nothing has to be fetched from the private archive, which a public reader cannot read. A selector run packs its own output at its end.

Applied in one pass to examples 341, 345, 347, 354 and 359: 16,376 files became 45 packs (37.0 MB to 0.9 MB), the twenty examples' records went from 22,103 files to 5,772, and no folder has more than 1,000 entries. Shown: each of the five handoffs (workflow_handoff.py handoff NNN, and --revision fix for 354 and 359) is byte for byte what it was; the five sealed originals restored from the store with artifacts.py fetch equal the packed records file for file (case_pack.py verify --against, 16,376 members); with one packed case of 359 removed, and then with one byte of it changed, its record became ineligible (does not exist; different raw checker output) while the other 39 established results stayed, and matched again with the pack put back; validate_example.py passes for the five. Not cut: the bytes of the large per-execution files (execution.json, 125 MB in 319 files), which are few and read whole; what to keep of them is a question about the evidence, for the user.

The budget: sync.py check reports more than 50 loose per-case files in one cases/ folder as an error that names the command, and more than 2,000 files under one example's records/ or 1,000 entries in one folder as a warning (none of either now; 50 ms). It also warns at 100 commits on neither develop nor main. The checkpoint's scan now reads a gzip blob as what it opens to, every member and whatever follows the last, and refuses one that opens to more than 256 MiB: without that, a credential inside a pack would have left unseen (POLICY 3, so each kept verdict is worked out once more).

Also in this commit, from the brief's acceptance table and VF-053: a test that kills the collector (SIGKILL) with a result's folder wiped and again with the result written, and collects again, with the earlier result sealed before the wipe; the watcher's private analysis reads an occurrence its machine never held from the store alone (shown on a disk store; on the real restricted bucket it is the watcher's to run); prune_workspaces.py counts a file as recoverable when the archive holds its exact bytes verified in the store, and its tests no longer read the machine's own archive; both run skills have the watcher say, with each verdict or merge, what waits on a person. VF-053 records what was done against each of its needs and stays open for the user.

### Keep the verification results index by day for results kept by day

change `quxwpwrrzunu` · [log `cab8a8886cd0`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/b9b56f5e-fc0e-48ca-a64e-7a46495d814f/cab8a8886cd012ad5489f2968644439f6875768132845bb2599fa7d2cab1a48d.jsonl.gz)

The brief's 'partition the result index': verification/results/index.json lists the results kept flat and names, under shards, each day that has results of its own; such a day has its own index.json with the same lines for its results. So once new jobs go by day the first file stops growing, and is the complete index of everything collected before the switch; a day's index is rewritten only by that day's collects. With no sharded result, as today, the file is byte for byte what the writer produced before (checked on the real 986 results: identical, 1,158,583 bytes).
